title: Strict coefficient reduction for proper image
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with positive quotients $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\mathfrak m_E^{n+1}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes, with completed coefficient sheaves $B_X,B_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Choose coefficient derived-system calculi $S_X,S_Y$, with reduction functors $r_X,r_Y$ and their prescribed evaluations [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data, def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $P_g$ for native varying-ring derived direct image [def-sp-varying-ring-operations], and $p_B,p_n$ for the completed and finite ringed derived direct images [def-strict-coefficient-ringed-geometric-data]. There is a natural transformation $\beta_g:p_Br_Y\to r_XP_g$ of functors on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B_X)$. Let $\rho_{W,n}:r_W\operatorname{ev}_n\simeq L(-\otimes_{B_W}A_n)$ be reductionEvaluation followed by inverse finiteReductionIso [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and let $e_{g,n}:P_g\operatorname{ev}_n\simeq\operatorname{ev}_np_n$ be native evaluation transported to the finite ringed presentation [def-weil-compact-support-native-system-evaluation]. For every ambient input $K$ and $n\geq0$, $\operatorname{ev}_n(\beta_g(K));e_{g,n}(r_XK)=\rho_{Y,n}(p_BK);\operatorname{properComparison}_n(K);p_n(\rho_{X,n}^{-1}(K))$. No assertion of invertibility of $\beta_g$ is made. The finite ringed presentation identifications are those of [lem-strict-coefficient-finite-geometric-coordinates].

source.place: First arrow of the Isomorphism paragraph; strict quotient-system refinement, Stacks 07A6, 0941 and 0B56

proof.text: Choose the existing strict-system operation models and their ordinary-limit/K-flat realization. Its push comparison t:P L_Y ≅ L_X p gives alpha_K=p(eta_X K);t^{-1}_{r_X K}. Define beta^0_K=r_Y(alpha_K);epsilon_Y(P r_X K). This is a natural transformation on all ambient completed inputs. Apply integralProperFiniteProjection at r_X K; naturality of finite scalar comparison and the reconstruction left triangle give the required finite-coordinate equation for beta^0.

For any two reduction calculi, adjoint uniqueness gives an isomorphism of their reductions. The unit_projection equation and injectivity of the finite scalar adjunction hom equivalence prove that this isomorphism intertwines their prescribed reductionEvaluation maps. Transport beta^0 to the chosen calculi SX,SY. Use nativeProperDerivedPresentation to transport the right direct-image model to the native one. Naturality of native evaluation and the two normalization equations give its finite constant-ring coordinate formula.

Unfold properFiniteReduction and strictCoefficientProperEvaluation. They use the same native-to-constant direct model and the same separately derived finiteDirectImage_eq. Naturality of that derived isomorphism, followed by its hom/inverse cancellation, converts the constant-ring formula to exactly the stated finite ringed-coordinate formula, with unchanged endpoints. No evaluation-faithfulness argument or invertibility of properComparison is used.

lean.statement:
theorem strictCoefficientProperReduction (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (SX : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (SY : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E Y) :
    ∃ β : push (completed l E) f ⋙ SY.reduction ⟶
        SX.reduction ⋙ ProEtale.VaryingRing.P (compactSupportSystemLevel l E)
          (compactSupportSystemQuotient l E) f,
      ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)) (n : ℕ),
        (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E Y n).map (β.app K) ≫
            (strictCoefficientProperEvaluation l E f n).hom.app (SX.reduction.obj K) =
          ((SY.reductionEvaluation n).hom.app ((push (completed l E) f).obj K) ≫
              (finiteReductionIso l E Y n).inv.app ((push (completed l E) f).obj K)) ≫
            (properComparison (reduction l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n)) f).app K ≫
            (push (finite l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n)) f).map
              ((finiteReductionIso l E X n).hom.app K ≫
                (SX.reductionEvaluation n).inv.app K)
